claim_impact: Weakens support for claim 'descriptive-market-dynamics' on the dimension 'tail_behavior'. Other dimensions are unaffected by this finding.
interpretation: The simulated distribution of 'Hill tail index (left)' is separated from the empirical reference (KS=0.77, adjusted p=0.003998 at the calibrated line). Note this metric also fails to separate the reference from block_bootstrap, garch_t; treat its pass/fail as one dimension of evidence, not a verdict.
observation: Across 6 non-overlapping simulated windows vs 124 reference windows, KS=0.766.
questions_for_author: Did we extract the model output correctly (frequency, units, log vs simple returns)?
Is matching the empirical distribution of 'Hill tail index (left)' within the intended use of the model?
Is there a configuration of the model under which this dimension is expected to match, and should we evaluate that configuration instead?
title: Hill tail index (left) diverges from the empirical reference
